headline: State action dispatch brief for residue management
briefing:
Where the units go: Of 500 units, the largest shares go to Sangrur (67 units), Tarn Taran (49 units), Fazilka (47 units), Ferozepur (45 units), and Bathinda (40 units). The other districts get smaller shares. The limit per district is 125 units.

Why: Sangrur has 215 forecast detections, with an 80% band from 66 to 439. That is more than the 147 detections of the last 3 days. Its likely burning is estimated at 437. The adjustment moves Fazilka from 25 units to 47 units.

How sure we are: The forecast is uncertain. Likely burning scales each forecast by the previous season's detection gap. The gap range behind Fazilka has low confidence. Likely burning is not a count of fires. What one unit achieves is assumed.

What to watch: Sangrur had 0.1 mm of rain in the last 3 days. The weather archive, standing in for a forecast, shows 0.0 mm for the next 3. Teams might start at cell 495 (central Sangrur), with 10 detections, and at cell 390 (central Sangrur), with 9 detections. The state says demand for straw machines falls almost entirely in the wheat sowing window of 15 to 20 days [K434].

results.title: Managing paddy straw without burning, in-situ and ex-situ options and machines
results.text:
# Why timing and placement matter

The state says the number of machines is enough for the paddy area by their field capacity, but almost all the demand falls in the wheat sowing window of 15 to 20 days, so a machine may not be available when a farmer wants it. Machines also wear out, and some are discarded every year. These are the state's own statements and have not been checked independently here.

results.title: Managing paddy straw without burning, in-situ and ex-situ options and machines
results.text:
# In-situ and ex-situ management

Punjab's status report of 26 November 2024 to the National Green Tribunal says paddy covers about 32 lakh hectares and leaves about 19.7 million tonnes of straw. In-situ management deals with the straw in the field, using seeding machines such as the super seeder to sow wheat. Ex-situ management collects the straw, mainly with balers, and takes it away for industrial and other uses. The state's action plan put in-situ management at 11.50 million tonnes in 2023 and 12.70 million tonnes (estimate) in 2024, ex-situ at 3.66 and 5.96 million tonnes, and fodder at 0.70 and 0.86 million tonnes.

results.title: Managing paddy straw without burning, in-situ and ex-situ options and machines
results.text:
# Machines and custom hiring

The report says 146,540 crop-residue machines, 61,951 of them super seeders, had been provided on subsidy under the Crop Residue Management scheme since 2018-19, including 2,183 balers and 2,039 rakes. Custom Hiring Centres are being promoted so that farmers do not have to buy the machinery and so that each machine is used closer to its capacity.

results.title: Why residue is burned in Punjab - the harvest to sowing window
results.text:
# Management options (in general terms)

- **In-situ management:** the residue is handled in the field, for example by machines that sow wheat directly through the straw (such as the Happy Seeder), or by mixing the straw into the soil.
- **Ex-situ management:** the straw is baled and removed from the field, then used for example as fuel in biomass plants and industry, or as fodder or packing material.

Both routes need machines, transport and a buyer or user for the straw. The cost and availability of these are a common part of the policy discussion.

get_gap_range.what_the_gap_is: the fall in fire counts per burned km2 since the base season; it is not the share of burning that is missed
get_gap_range.changes_in_words: counts fell 86.0% and burned area rose 14.3%
get_gap_range.methods: S-NPP detections against burned area, base season 2022; official counts against burned area, base season 2022 (start date not stated); S-NPP detections against burned area, base season 2023; official counts against burned area, base season 2023 (start date not stated)
get_gap_range.direction: counts fell more than burned area
get_gap_range.timing_evidence: Punjab-wide only. Night share of S-NPP detections: 1.6% (95% interval 1.4% to 1.9%) in 2024 against 0.2% (0.1% to 0.2%) in 2022: supports a shift in timing. MODIS change relative to the S-NPP change since 2022: 1.91 times (rule: at least 1.5): supports a shift in timing. MODIS passes at other times (Terra in the morning, Aqua drifting later in the afternoon), which is a confound.
get_gap_range.other_explanations: A fall in detections per burned area fits three explanations: burning moved outside satellite pass times, fires became smaller or cooler, or the sensitivity of the burned-area product changed.
get_gap_range.caveat: The range shows only how the result changes with the count series and the base season. It does not include the error of the MODIS burned-area product, which is unknown and is the largest uncertainty. This is triangulation of satellite and official signals, not field verification.
get_gap_range.used_for: This is the previous season's range, which scales this season's forecast. A negative value is treated as no adjustment.
